# Controller-Based vs  Minimal APIs

These are **two different architectural patterns** for building APIs in .NET. Let me break down the differences.

- [Controller-based WebAPI Example](https://github.com/Lightbridge-KS/PatientWebApiDtoExample)

## Two Approaches

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│           .NET Web API Patterns                     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                     │
│  1. Controller-Based (Traditional)                 │
│     └── Uses Classes + Attributes                  │
│                                                     │
│  2. Minimal APIs (Modern)                          │
│     └── Uses Direct Route Mapping                  │
│                                                     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 1. Controller-Based Approach (What You Saw)


**Structure:**
```
Controllers/
│
└── PatientsController.cs
    │
    ├── [ApiController]        ← Class-level attribute
    ├── [Route("api/...")]     ← Class-level routing
    │
    ├── [HttpGet] GetAll()     ← Method-level attribute
    ├── [HttpGet("{id}")] ...  ← Method-level routing
    └── [HttpPost] Create()
```

**Code Example:**
```csharp
// Controllers/PatientsController.cs
[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class PatientsController : ControllerBase
{
    [HttpGet]
    public ActionResult<List<PatientRecord>> GetAll()
    {
        return Ok(patients);
    }

    [HttpGet("{id}")]
    public ActionResult<PatientRecord> GetById(int id)
    {
        return Ok(patient);
    }
}
```

**Program.cs (minimal setup):**
```csharp
var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

builder.Services.AddControllers();  // Register controller services

var app = builder.Build();

app.MapControllers();  // Map all controllers automatically

app.Run();
```

## 2. Minimal APIs Approach


**Structure:**
```
Program.cs
│
├── app.MapGet("/api/patients", ...)
├── app.MapGet("/api/patients/{id}", ...)
├── app.MapPost("/api/patients", ...)
└── ... (all routes in one file or organized by extension methods)
```

**Code Example:**
```csharp
// Program.cs
var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

var app = builder.Build();

// In-memory data
var patients = new List<PatientRecord>
{
    new PatientRecord(1, "John Doe", new DateTime(1980, 5, 15), "M"),
    new PatientRecord(2, "Jane Smith", new DateTime(1992, 8, 22), "F")
};

// GET: /api/patients
app.MapGet("/api/patients", () =>
{
    return Results.Ok(new PatientListDto
    {
        Patients = patients,
        TotalCount = patients.Count
    });
});

// GET: /api/patients/{id}
app.MapGet("/api/patients/{id}", (int id) =>
{
    var patient = patients.FirstOrDefault(p => p.Id == id);
    return patient is not null 
        ? Results.Ok(patient) 
        : Results.NotFound();
});

// POST: /api/patients
app.MapPost("/api/patients", (CreatePatientDto dto) =>
{
    var newId = patients.Max(p => p.Id) + 1;
    var newPatient = new PatientRecord(newId, dto.Name, dto.BirthDate, dto.Gender);
    patients.Add(newPatient);
    
    return Results.Created($"/api/patients/{newId}", newPatient);
});

app.Run();
```

## Key Differences


| Aspect | Controller-Based | Minimal APIs |
|--------|------------------|--------------|
| **File Organization** | Separate controller classes | Routes in Program.cs (or organized via extension methods) |
| **Syntax** | Object-oriented (classes + methods) | Functional (delegates/lambdas) |
| **Boilerplate** | More code, more structure | Less code, more concise |
| **Discoverability** | Easy (all routes in one class) | Can be harder (routes scattered) |
| **Testability** | Easy (standard class testing) | Need different approach |
| **Dependency Injection** | Constructor injection | Parameter injection |
| **Filters/Middleware** | Built-in attribute filters | Manual configuration |
| **Best For** | Large, complex APIs | Small to medium APIs, microservices |

## Comparison Side-by-Side


### Controller-Based (GET endpoint)

```csharp
[ApiController]
[Route("api/[controller]")]
public class PatientsController : ControllerBase
{
    private readonly IPatientService _service;
    
    // Constructor injection
    public PatientsController(IPatientService service)
    {
        _service = service;
    }
    
    [HttpGet("{id}")]
    public ActionResult<PatientRecord> GetById(int id)
    {
        var patient = _service.GetById(id);
        if (patient == null)
            return NotFound();
        return Ok(patient);
    }
}
```

### Minimal API (same endpoint)

```csharp
// In Program.cs
app.MapGet("/api/patients/{id}", 
    (int id, IPatientService service) =>  // Parameter injection
    {
        var patient = service.GetById(id);
        return patient is not null 
            ? Results.Ok(patient) 
            : Results.NotFound();
    });
```

## When to Use Each?


### Use Controller-Based When:

✅ Building large, enterprise applications  
✅ Need complex authorization/authentication  
✅ Team prefers OOP and traditional patterns  
✅ Want built-in model validation attributes  
✅ Need action filters (`[Authorize]`, custom filters)  
✅ Coming from ASP.NET Framework background


### Use Minimal APIs When:

✅ Building microservices or small APIs  
✅ Prototyping quickly  
✅ Performance is critical (slightly faster)  
✅ Want less ceremony and boilerplate  
✅ Team prefers functional programming style  
✅ Starting a new greenfield project


## Hybrid Approach (Organizing Minimal APIs)


For larger Minimal API projects, you can organize routes using extension methods:

**Program.cs:**
```csharp
var app = builder.Build();

app.MapPatientEndpoints();  // Extension method
app.MapDicomEndpoints();    // Another group

app.Run();
```

**PatientEndpoints.cs:**
```csharp
public static class PatientEndpoints
{
    public static void MapPatientEndpoints(this WebApplication app)
    {
        var group = app.MapGroup("/api/patients")
            .WithTags("Patients");
        
        group.MapGet("/", GetAll);
        group.MapGet("/{id}", GetById);
        group.MapPost("/", Create);
    }
    
    private static IResult GetAll()
    {
        // Implementation
    }
    
    private static IResult GetById(int id)
    {
        // Implementation
    }
}
```

## My Recommendation for You


Since you're learning C# and coming from Dart/Flutter:

1. **Start with Controller-Based** - it's more similar to class-based patterns you know
2. **Understand Minimal APIs** - good to know for small projects
3. **Choose based on project size**:
   - Small API → Minimal APIs
   - Medium/Large API → Controllers
